Source: `terms/OT2002/records/Citizens-Bank-v-Alafabco-Inc_summary-merits_2003-06-02.md`.

Commercial restructurings with the demonstrated connection to actual multistate business satisfy §2 without separate substantial-effects proof for each instrument. The proponent must establish the real commercial connection before aggregate magnitude can matter. State courts then apply the existing agreement, delegation, preservation, and ordinary-defense rules to the actual arbitration request.

### 2003-06-16 — Star Scientific, Inc. v. Beales

Source: `terms/OT2002/records/Star-Scientific-Inc-v-Beales_merits_2003-06-16.md`.

Virginia's challenged statute may require the defined reserve for qualifying consumer sales made directly or through intermediaries. The economic classification is sustained on the complete payment, conduct, and retained-property arrangements. Its local-sales measure and described tracing burdens survive the distinct Commerce inquiries, and the associated settlement requires no congressional consent under the governing federal-supremacy rule.

A concrete assessment must follow the statutory sales base. Access to principal and mandatory return are governed by the distinct B1–B3 conditions in Holding 2, including B1's claim and claimant limits and B2's manufacturer showing and Commonwealth-share calculation. A supported materially different discriminatory, territorial, or operational application receives review under its own facts and the applicable constitutional standard.

### 2002-11-04 — Early v. Packer

Source: `terms/OT2002/records/Early-v-Packer_summary-merits_2002-11-04.md`.

Chief Justice Stone-Zsela agrees with the governing legal rules but dissents from their application. He regards the judge’s public repetition of the majority’s criticism as giving that criticism judicial force. Coupled with individualized pressure on an exhausted juror and disclosure of the 11-to-1 division, the intervention communicated a demand to yield even without naming the desired verdict. Permission to disagree could not neutralize that combined pressure.

Applying Lowenfield’s contextual rule, he finds actual coercion and separately concludes under Williams that the state assessment was objectively unreasonable, not merely less persuasive. He rejects both a constitutional citation requirement and reliance on Jenkins or Gypsum as independent state constitutional commands. His ground is the sustained exercise of judicial authority in this record, not a categorical ban on supplemental instructions, numerical knowledge or legitimate health inquiries. He would preserve a conditional writ allowing California a reasonable period to retry only the counts whose verdicts followed the coercive intervention, leaving earlier sealed verdicts and acquittals untouched.

### 2002-11-04 — Woodford v. Visciotti

Source: `terms/OT2002/records/Woodford-v-Visciotti_summary-merits_2002-11-04.md`.

Chief Justice Stone-Zsela joins the governing rules but dissents from the result. He agrees that occasional use of probable does not independently establish a contrary-to violation. His objection concerns what the state court actually did with the mitigating account. The missing coherent history of abuse, instability and functional impairment, combined with counsel’s damaging presentation, could affect a conscientious juror’s sentencing judgment even though it did not excuse the crimes. Scattered guilt-phase brain-injury evidence did not necessarily perform that explanatory work.

He gives the killing, attempted killing and prior violence their full aggravating force, but concludes that the combined impairment of the mitigation presentation undermines confidence in the sentence. In his view, treating the grave offenses as a sufficient answer to that impairment materially understates lawful mitigation and makes the state application objectively unreasonable under Williams as well as prejudicial under Strickland. The deliberations and questions reinforce the materiality of the missing account without proving any juror’s hypothetical choice.

He would preserve conditional sentence relief, allowing a reasonable period for constitutionally adequate resentencing or a lawful noncapital disposition. Any properly preserved unresolved defense that counsel performed adequately must be decided before implementing a writ dependent on deficiency. The convictions remain intact. He adopts no categorical prejudice rule for abuse, brain injury, lengthy deliberation or capital cases.

### 2002-12-10 — Howsam v. Dean Witter Reynolds, Inc.

Source: `terms/OT2002/records/Howsam-v-Dean-Witter-Reynolds-Inc_merits_2002-12-10.md`.

Thomas concurs in the judgment under the agreement's express selection of New York law for construction and enforcement. Volt requires respect for that choice. Smith Barney Shearson, Inc. v. Sacharow treats this kind of eligibility issue as substantive arbitrability, ordinarily for courts, but finds a clear delegation in the broad agreement combined with NASD Rule 10324. The actual client agreement and incorporated Code establish that delegation here. Thomas does not adopt the Court's general federal procedural presumption. Sacharow distinguishes a contractual eligibility rule from the statutory-limitations issue in Matter of Smith Barney, Harris Upham & Co. v. Luckie; no omission of the word enforcement or later Dean Witter signature supplies his ground.

### 2003-01-13 — Montiel v. Davis

Source: `terms/OT2002/records/Montiel-v-Davis_merits_2003-01-13.md`.

Thomas, joined by Scalia, concurs in Part I and the judgment. Consistently with the statutory construction he maintained in Holder, De Grandy, Page, and Balderas, he concludes that §2 does not authorize the asserted judicial allocation of districts. That antecedent construction supplies his reason to affirm the statutory judgment; it is not a join in the Court's Gingles and totality analysis. He also withholds assent from Part II's territorial-design rule. His agreement with the independently sufficient constitutional evidentiary disposition does not adopt that broader rule.

### 2003-01-14 — Sattazahn v. Pennsylvania

Source: `terms/OT2002/records/Sattazahn-v-Pennsylvania_merits_2003-01-14.md`.

**Stone-Zsela, concurring.** He joins the double-jeopardy holding and would independently reach the same sentence-only result under due process. Pennsylvania made life the conclusive consequence of its completed unsuccessful capital opportunity. Requiring surrender of that final limit to correct guilt-phase error burdens meaningful appellate review and upsets the adjudicated liberty interest without a new lawful basis. Guilt retrial and life punishment remain available; the appeal alone cannot recreate capital exposure the completed process ended. Hicks supplies protection for an actual sentencing entitlement, while this application develops its operation in the distinct final-life setting. The position does not presume prosecutorial vindictiveness from a harsher sentence, preserve every favorable sentencing term after reversal, or convert the jury's division into an acquittal. The other four majority Justices rest on the sufficient double-jeopardy ground and do not join this independent theory.

**O'Connor, joined by Scalia, Kennedy and Thomas, dissenting.** They would affirm rejection of both federal challenges. Bullington and Rumsey protect an adjudication that death is unavailable on the merits. Here neither the jury nor the judge found the State's aggravation proof insufficient or selected life on the merits. The statutory consequence of deadlock therefore supplies no federal acquittal finality once the defendant obtains reversal of the underlying conviction for trial error. Poland preserves that distinction, and Richardson permits retrial of unresolved allegations. The State must still obtain the lawful findings and comply with the procedures governing the new capital proceeding. Hicks protects the entitlement state law actually confers, but the supplied law establishes no life ceiling independently surviving reversal of the conviction. Their due-process rejection concerns that asserted entitlement, not every possible state-created sentencing interest. O'Connor and Kennedy do not adopt the separate element-based explanation below.

**Scalia, joined by Thomas, additionally dissenting.** Even if a necessary present-offense aggravator performs the constitutional work of an element, a hung jury has not rejected it. Their Monge position concerns a completed failure of proof in an element adjudication; Apprendi, Angle, Harris and Ring supply present-offense factfinding protections without treating deadlock as acquittal. They therefore agree with the common dissent and explain why its result survives this limited element analysis. They adopt no universal prior-conviction exception, proposition that every aggravator is a separate offense, or rule that eligibility requires selection of death. O'Connor and Kennedy join no part of this additional writing.

### 2003-02-25 — Miller-El v. Cockrell

Source: `terms/OT2002/records/Miller-El-v-Cockrell_merits_2003-02-25.md`.

Miller-El v. Cockrell, February 25, 2003 — Scalia concurs, joined by no other Justice, and joins the Court's opinion in full. Certification requires reasonable debate about the district court's application of AEDPA, not merely debate about the abstract constitutional claim. An indisputable statutory bar would defeat issuance. Although the cumulative record barely warrants appellate consideration in his assessment, the individualized reasons and substantial State evidence remain powerful merits arguments. His certificate vote expresses no conclusion that those explanations are implausible or that a writ should issue. This assessment is noncontrolling.

Miller-El v. Cockrell, February 25, 2003 — Thomas dissents, joined by no other Justice. He reads the certificate determination as part of the proceeding covered by §2254(e)(1), requiring actual clear-and-convincing rebuttal of the state factual finding before this fact-dependent Batson claim becomes reasonably debatable. Slack's different statutory context does not settle that issue for him. He finds no adequate rebuttal: historical practice and shuffles do not show pretext for the particular strikes, juror comparisons must account for the prosecutor's combined reasons, and the individualized explanations for questioning and strikes support the findings. A Batson hearing occurring two years after voir dire does not by itself reduce the statutory presumption. He additionally doubts the showing under the majority's standard but retains the distinct statutory objection as his principal ground. He would affirm the certificate denial. These positions are noncontrolling.

### 2003-03-05 — Lockyer v. Andrade

Source: `terms/OT2002/records/Lockyer-v-Andrade_merits_2003-03-05.md`.

Lockyer v. Andrade, March 5, 2003: O'Connor's partial dissent, joined by Scalia, Kennedy and Thomas, accepts the statutory framework and full aggregate but considers the state result a reasonable application of the earlier law in light of serious recidivism, separate crimes and parole possibility. It would deny the writ without affirmatively deciding the sentence's constitutionality on direct review. Scalia and Thomas's join is statutory and does not endorse the proportionality foundation. ### 2003-04-07 — PacifiCare Health Systems, Inc. v. Book

Source: `terms/OT2002/records/PacifiCare-Health-Systems-Inc-v-Book_merits_2003-04-07.md`.

**Stone-Zsela, concurring in the judgment.** The Chief Justice would ordinarily vacate and remand for agreement-specific judicial examination of a concrete claim that the compelled forum disables an essential federal remedy. The objector must identify an actual restriction; the proponent must establish the agreement and any valid, clear and unmistakable delegation covering that objection. A preserved challenge to the delegation itself remains judicial. Broad arbitration language and Howsam's forum-timing presumption do not establish delegation of this distinct question.

Absent such a delegation, he would have the court construe the actual agreements and incorporated terms, develop only genuinely material preserved disputes that prevent decision, and determine whether each restriction eliminates an essential remedy. A sufficient contractual record calls for decision without an unnecessary hearing. Mastrobuono requires contextual reading, and RICO trebling cannot be excluded merely by labeling it punitive. A preserving agreement would be enforced. A clear disabling term would require lawful severance under the bargain and ordinary law before compulsion; if no lawful arbitral forum remains, litigation would continue in court. This rule would extend First Options and Green Tree's protection of effective statutory access while keeping Howsam's ordinary procedural category intact. A valid delegation would change the initial decisionmaker, with later review confined to an independently authorized route.

Because the Court treats the particular disputed restrictions as arbitral merits construction, he accepts reversal of a refusal to compel resting solely on assumed exclusion. His agreement preserves an actually available lawful challenge to a construction eliminating federal entitlement, subject to the authority and conditions governing that challenge; ambiguity does not permanently insulate a disabling construction. He joins the judgment on that narrower basis and does not join the Court's allocation rationale. His preferred judicial-gateway rule is a distinct proposed ground, not the Court's holding.

### 2003-05-19 — Price v. Vincent

Source: `terms/OT2002/records/Price-v-Vincent_merits_2003-05-19.md`.

Stone-Zsela's May 19, 2003 opinion concurring in part and dissenting in part supplies a noncontrolling application: the actual grant, judicial acknowledgement and contemporaneous entry establish a completed substantive acquittal on this whole record, making Michigan's provisional characterization objectively unreasonable rather than merely less persuasive. His proposed conditional writ removes only the first-degree conviction, sentence and attributable custody, bars reprosecution of that acquitted charge and preserves lawful remaining dispositions. His express reasonable-state-reading alternative remains a substantive conditional limit, not a concession caused by the vote. He uses neither Sattazahn's later rule nor his separate due-process rationale as 1997 clearly established law. Every published qualification appears in Public Projection / Separate Writings. No Associate publishes a separate opinion, and no unadjudicated Supreme Court event is carried by this remand.

### 2003-06-16 — Star Scientific, Inc. v. Beales

Source: `terms/OT2002/records/Star-Scientific-Inc-v-Beales_merits_2003-06-16.md`.

Justice Scalia concurs in part and in the judgment. He joins the standing, economic, actual territorial, and Compact holdings. For the remaining Commerce challenge, he follows his narrower West Lynn Creamery and Walsh position: judicial invalidation is available for facial geographic discrimination or a materially identical arrangement already invalidated by the Court. This scheme satisfies neither description. A preference for settlement participants is not facial discrimination by geographic origin, and the local-sales escrow lacks the prohibited outside-price command or dedicated local-producer subsidy. He therefore supports affirmance while withholding assent to free-standing Pike balancing.

Justice Thomas concurs in part and in the judgment. He joins the same stated portions, including the conclusion that this local-sales measure does not impose the asserted outside-transaction control. Consistent with his Walsh position, he rejects the negative Commerce Clause—the inferred restriction on state legislation when Congress has not acted—as an independent judicial limitation. That constitutional ground supplies his vote for dismissal of the remaining Commerce claim. He does not join Pike balancing or treat ordinary economic rationality as its substitute.
